measured_effect.what_this_does_not_claim: That the zero live set on 13 rows is a statement about possibility: it is a statement about this closure. That 2 is a ceiling on ambiguity: it is what one row and one suite supplied. That the 15 structural edits are failures: they are outside the instrument and are censused.

next_step: Build the perturbation harness, not a bigger grammar: at the site, re-run the failing test with one input perturbed so the postcondition flips, and admit only candidates whose value changes with the perturbation. Acceptance: live-set size >= 1 on >= 8 of 15 in-class rows, the number of distinct green rules must fall to 1, and every verified patch must still name a frame-bound value.
real_outcome: 150,809 to 154,157 candidates are offered per row. On 13 of 15 in-class rows ZERO of them produce the demanded value, so the binding failure on this corpus is coverage, not over-permissiveness -- the opposite of what the identifiability worry predicts. On the one row the instrument can verify, 2 candidates do, and the suite accepts BOTH as green: two syntactically different rules, indistinguishable because the test supplies exactly one name. One row runs the site 109 times inside a single failing test and that is not a contrast set: the demand is due at one execution and the other 108 assumed the original value everywhere.

obs_solution.efficiency_mechanism: Ordering and exact fit replace breadth: 409 flips decided 15 commits, and no candidate refinement was scored, ranked or thresholded.
obs_solution.generality_mechanism: The rewrite is generic Python AST plus a counter; the oracle is the project's own pytest; the address is a site and a firing, so it carries to any executable artifact.
obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Message channel: 1 of 15 at the line, 0 at the expression. Whole-predicate flips: cannot express a guard that is right once and wrong once. Scoring: unnecessary once fit is exact. Stored state: costlier than re-measuring in ~50 microseconds.
